reply.title: Why does a sigmoid squash any number into 0 to 1?
reply.story:
When modeling probabilities or neural network activations, we often need to take any real number from negative to positive infinity and map it cleanly between zero and one. Linear scalings fail because they extend infinitely, but an exponential growth ratio creates a natural saturation. By dividing an exponential by one plus itself, we build the classic sigmoid curve.

As the input grows very large positively, the exponential term dominates and pushes the output toward one. As the input drops toward negative infinity, the exponential term vanishes and leaves the output near zero. The steepness parameter controls how rapidly this transition happens around the central midpoint.
